title: KV260 AXI-Lite slave simulation — RTL protocol compliance verified, on-hardware hang narrowed to infrastructure
context: On-hardware Exp 661 wedged the KV260 PS twice. Hypothesis: the AXI-Lite state machine in ising_sampler_v2.v line 325-352 deadlocks when AW and W channels arrive on different cycles. This simulation tested that hypothesis directly and REJECTED it.
hypothesis_rejected: AXI-Lite state machine deadlocks on split AW/W channels — the state machine correctly waits for both VALIDs to coincide and acknowledges in 2 cycles regardless of interleaving. The on-hardware hang is NOT in the AXI protocol logic.

remaining_hypotheses_for_hang.description: pl_clk0 not actually running on-hardware despite xmutil loadapp success — overlay's fclk_cfg fragment did not activate the clock. PL has no ACLK, slave's clocked always-block never fires, ACK never asserts, PS AXI master blocks forever.
remaining_hypotheses_for_hang.evidence: Matches observed symptom (first access hangs the whole PS). Simulation assumes ACLK is toggling; hardware might not.
remaining_hypotheses_for_hang.next_experiment: On Kria, after xmutil loadapp, probe /sys/class/fclk/fclk0/ state AND read CRL_APB PL0_REF_CTRL register via devmem2 to confirm pl_clk0 is actually running at 40 MHz before any AXI access.

remaining_hypotheses_for_hang.description: AXI SmartConnect upstream of the sampler has a protocol-violation monitor that hangs the PS interconnect on some edge case not reproduced in a bare-DUT testbench.
remaining_hypotheses_for_hang.evidence: SmartConnect is authored by Xilinx; protocol monitors are aggressive by default. This testbench connects directly to the sampler with no SmartConnect in the loop.
remaining_hypotheses_for_hang.next_experiment: Extend testbench to instantiate an axi_protocol_checker (or hand-code one) between the master BFM and the sampler to catch any subtle protocol errors.

remaining_hypotheses_for_hang.description: Dynamic power integrity — 128 LFSRs + 128 sigmoid LUTs + 128 DSP multipliers switching simultaneously exceeds K26 power envelope on a cold start.
remaining_hypotheses_for_hang.evidence: N=64 build uses 1088 DSPs (87% of XCK26 budget). Simultaneous activation on first cycle could cause a supply droop that corrupts PS registers.
remaining_hypotheses_for_hang.next_experiment: Add a 16-cycle 'warmup' sequence to the RTL that staggers LFSR enable signals across 16 cycles to spread the switching current. Cheap RTL change, would rule this out.

remaining_hypotheses_for_hang.description: ARESETN held low — dfx-mgr did not release reset, state machine is parked and ACK never asserts.
remaining_hypotheses_for_hang.evidence: Less likely: dfx-mgr's reset-release is standard and well-tested. But trivial to verify from on-kria probe.
remaining_hypotheses_for_hang.next_experiment: On-kria, read the pl_resetn0 signal state via the proc_sys_reset AXI handle (or inspect /sys/bus/platform output).

retro_074_progress: RTL AXI protocol hypothesis rejected (1 of 4 hypotheses eliminated). Next hypothesis to test: pl_clk0 not running. Does NOT require power-cycling the board — the fclk state probe is read-only.
